faqs.question: What is the Well Plate Illuminator used for?
faqs.answer: It's a high-throughput LED exposure system built for simultaneous, uniform irradiation of samples across a standard 24-well plate.

faqs.question: How does WPI keep illumination consistent across all 24 wells?
faqs.answer: Each well has its own dedicated LED paired with a custom optical guide and lens, aimed precisely into that well rather than shared across the whole plate.

faqs.question: How is light intensity controlled without changing the wavelength?

sections.glanceDescription: Compare WPI's optics, cooling, wavelength range, and application fit.
sections.intro: WPI is built around a problem every high-throughput photochemistry screen runs into: getting the same light to land on well 1 and well 24 equally. A single light source spread across a plate almost never manages it. Twenty-four individual LEDs, one per well, each with its own optical guide and lens, does.
paragraphs: Illumination comes from below rather than above, running straight through a transparent plate or vial bottom. That same bottom-up design lets 4 mL auto-sampler vials drop directly into the plate format when the workflow calls for it, without switching to a different instrument.

Heat management runs on two fronts at once: the anodized aluminum body dissipates heat passively, and an integrated cooling fan keeps operating temperature stable through longer experiments, important with 24 LEDs running simultaneously rather than one.

sections.eyebrow: Wavelength Selection and PWM Intensity Control
sections.title: Wavelength Selection and PWM Intensity Control
sections.tabSummary: Choosing wavelength and dialing in intensity
body: Getting the right wavelength is only half the job in a screening experiment. The other half is controlling intensity without accidentally changing the wavelength that was just selected.

Nine wavelength options cover near UV through far red, plus lime and cool white as broad-spectrum choices, all fully characterized so exactly what's being delivered is never a guess. The optional PWM dimmer module solves the intensity problem specifically: instead of reducing current to dim the LED, which can shift its emission wavelength, PWM adjusts the duty cycle, how long the LED stays on during each rapid switching cycle, so spectral output stays exactly where it started even as irradiance changes.

heroParagraphs: Running a photochemistry screen across a whole plate usually means one light source trying to cover 24 wells evenly, and it rarely does. WPI takes a different approach: every well gets its own LED.

Each of the 24 LEDs pairs with a custom optical guide and lens aimed directly into its corresponding well, so neighboring samples don't cross-contaminate each other's exposure and every position gets the same irradiance. Light comes from below, straight through transparent well plates or vials, and if the workflow already runs on 4 mL auto-sampler vials, they drop right into the plate format instead of requiring a container switch.

Nine wavelength options span near UV through far red and broad-spectrum white, and the optional PWM dimmer module fine-tunes intensity without shifting spectral output, ideal for kinetic studies and photoredox screening where the wavelength has to stay exactly where it's set.
